key_insight: Composition-tuned site disorder in quaternary Heusler NiRuMnGa frustrates magnetic exchange, stabilizing a cluster-glass state instead of long-range magnetic order.
engineering_relevance: This shows how controlled antisite disorder in Heusler alloys can be used to tune low-temperature magnetic behavior, which is relevant for functional magnetic materials and spintronic design.
method: First-principles calculations to identify the energetically favorable crystal structure.
Powder X-ray diffraction refinement using the computed structure as the model.
Magnetic characterization via dc/AC susceptibility, hysteresis, relaxation, and memory measurements.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports B2-type Ni/Ru and Mn/Ga disorder, ZFC-FC irreversibility near 48 K that shifts with field, unsaturated magnetization up to 7 T, and no heat-capacity anomaly near the transition.
watch_item: Because the magnetic response is strongly disorder-dependent, the inferred cluster-glass state may vary with composition, sample homogeneity, and degree of antisite mixing.
paper_title: Role of composition-tuned disorder on magnetic exchange interactions in NiRuMnGa
